Doc Id: SEC-RB-ACCESS · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2025-09-01 · Owner: Information Security · Classification: internal

Access Requests Runbook

1. Purpose

This runbook explains how employees request access to Kranich Route Cloud and the internal tools we rely on every day. It covers new access, changes to existing access, and what happens when an account is locked.

We keep access management simple and transparent. Whether you are joining Kranich, changing teams, or taking on a new responsibility, this runbook tells you what to do. If something is unclear, reach out to it-help@kranich.example and we will point you in the right direction.

Our goal is to make sure everyone has the access they need to do their work — and no more. This keeps our customers' data safe and our systems easy to manage.

2. Requesting access

Access requests are handled through a short form on the Grove intranet. You will find the link under "IT & Security" in the policy library. The form asks for your name, your team, the system you need access to, and a brief reason.

Most access is granted by your manager or a team lead. For example, when Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, joins a new project in Routing Core, her engineering manager approves the request for the relevant repositories and environments. For customer-facing systems, the Customer Success team follows the same process.

If you need access to a system that is not listed on the form, select "Other" and describe what you need. The Information Security team will review your request and follow up with you directly.

Access changes follow the same path. When you move teams — say, from Fleet Insights to Platform & Infrastructure — submit a new request for the systems you need in your new role. Your old access is removed as part of the change, so you do not need to ask for that separately.

When you leave Kranich or go on a long absence, your manager notifies People & Culture, and access is revoked promptly.

2. Baseline Every device that Kranich issues — whether a laptop, a desktop, or a mobile device — must be enrolled in our device management solution before it is used for work. Enrollment happens as part of the onboarding process, and it ensures that the device receives our standard security configuration, can be located if lost, and can be remotely wiped if necessary. The baseline configuration for all company-managed endpoints includes the following requirements: •  A strong device password or biometric authentication must be enabled. Screen lock must engage automatically after a short period of inactivity. •  Full disk encryption must be active, as described in §3 of this standard. •  Automatic updates must be enabled for the operating system and for all approved software. •  Firewall software must be turned on and configured to block unsolicited inbound connections. •  Company-approved antivirus or endpoint detection and response software must be installed and running. •  Browsers must be configured to block pop-ups and to warn against unsafe downloads. •  Administrative (root or administrator) access on the device must be limited to what your role genuinely requires. If you need administrator rights for development or testing, request them through it-help@kranich.example, and they will be granted on a case-by-case basis. Example: Marek, a field solutions engineer who works with clients in Poland, receives a new laptop before an on-site workshop. During onboarding, the device is enrolled, encrypted, and configured with the standard firewall and antivirus settings. When he later needs to install a specialized network diagnostic tool for a client demonstration, he requests administrator access through it-help, which is granted for a limited purpose and then reviewed. Personal devices are not a substitute for company-managed hardware when company data is involved. If you occasionally need to check email or calendar from a personal phone, that is acceptable provided the device has a passcode and the latest operating system. However, personal devices must never be used to store customer data or to access the Kranich Route Cloud production environment. If you are unsure whether a particular task is appropriate for a personal device, ask your manager or security@kranich.example before proceeding. Lost or stolen devices must be reported to it-help@kranich.example immediately.

context_blocks.header: [38] SEC-STD-DATACLASS.pdf — Data Classification Standard > 3. Handling rules > Transmission (p. 3)
context_blocks.text:
Transmission

You may send public data through any channel. You may send internal data through standard Kranich channels, including email and chat. For confidential data, use only the approved file- sharing or email systems, and consider whether encryption is required. For restricted data, do not transmit it through email or chat at all. Use the approved mechanism, such as the secrets vault or a secure transfer tool, and confirm the recipient before sending.

If you receive confidential or restricted data through an unapproved channel, do not open attachments or follow links. Notify security@kranich.example promptly.

Access

Access to data must follow the principle of least privilege. Give people access only to the data they need for their current role. When someone changes teams or leaves Kranich, revoke or adjust their access promptly. Use the access review process that the Platform & Infrastructure team runs.

Never share your login credentials with anyone. Use 1Password to store your passwords and never reuse a password across systems. If you suspect that your credentials have been compromised, change them immediately and report the incident to security@kranich.example.

Example: Ines Duarte, an engineering manager in Berlin, welcomes a new member to the Routing Core team. She requests access to the routing repository for the new hire and verifies that the departing team member's access has been removed.

Retention and destruction

Keep data only as long as you need it for a legitimate business purpose. Follow the retention schedules defined in the relevant policies, such as POL-004 for personnel records. When data is no longer needed, delete it using the approved method. For paper documents that contain confidential or restricted data, shred them rather than discarding them in the regular trash.

When you leave Kranich or change roles, return or destroy any confidential or restricted data that you no longer need. If you are unsure whether you may keep a document, ask your manager.

context_blocks.header: [39] POL-008-v1.0.pdf — Parental Leave Policy > 7. Returning to work (p. 3)
context_blocks.text:
7. Returning to work

We will agree on your return date before your leave starts, and we will confirm it in writing. If you want to change that date, please let People & Culture know as soon as possible so we can adjust plans.

About two weeks before your return, your manager will reach out to schedule a reintegration conversation. This is a chance to catch up on what happened while you were away, to discuss any changes to the team or the product, and to plan your first weeks back. You will also receive a short update from your team so that you do not feel lost on day one.

Your first days back should be gentle. We suggest that you start with a half day or a short week, if that helps, and we encourage you to ease into your workload. Your manager will help you prioritize and will make sure you are not overwhelmed.

When you return, you will find that your accounts and access are still active. If you notice any issue, contact it-help@kranich.example and we will resolve it promptly.

Example: Sofia returned from her leave on a Wednesday. Her manager had scheduled a reintegration meeting for Thursday morning, and her team had prepared a written summary of recent decisions. By the following week, Sofia felt up to date and ready to take back her responsibilities.

8. Questions

If you have any questions about this policy, please reach out to People & Culture at people@kranich.example. Lea, our people operations specialist, can help you understand the process, and Aylin Demir, our VP People & Culture, is available for more complex conversations.

For questions about how your leave interacts with local law in your country, we can connect you with the relevant information or, where needed, with external advice. We want you to feel confident and supported throughout your parental leave journey.

If you have concerns about confidentiality or fairness, you can also contact security@kranich.example, and we will treat your query with discretion. We are here to help, and we thank you for being part of the Kranich community.

context_blocks.header: [40] POL-007-v1.0.pdf — Sick Leave & Medical Absence > 5. Returning to work (p. 2–3)
context_blocks.text:
5. Returning to work

When you are ready to return, please let your manager know at least a day in advance. This gives your team time to prepare and helps you ease back in.

You do not need a doctor's certificate to confirm you are fit to work after a short illness. For longer absences, your doctor may recommend a gradual return, for example reduced hours or modified duties for a period. Please discuss this with your manager and People & Culture. We will do our best to accommodate medical recommendations where operationally possible.

If you return from an absence that lasted several weeks, we suggest scheduling a short catch- up with your manager. This is an opportunity to review any changes that happened while you were away, prioritise your work, and agree on how to handle anything that accumulated. We do not expect you to catch up on everything at once.

Example: Sofia, a product manager in Fleet Insights working remotely from Spain, returns after a two-week absence. Her manager schedules a thirty-minute video call to bring her up to speed. Together they agree that she will focus on one key deliverable for the first week rather than trying to cover everything.

If you have a chronic condition that causes recurring absences, please let People & Culture know if you feel comfortable doing so. We can discuss workplace adjustments that might help you manage your health while working. Any information you share is treated confidentially.

question: What is the standard equipment budget and at what write-off threshold is no separate approval needed?
expected_answer: The equipment budget for a standard role is €2,200. (the restricted part is not available at this access level)
answer_text:
**Standard equipment budget:** The current Equipment & Hardware Policy (POL-006 v2.2, effective 2025-05-01) sets a €2,200 budget for a Standard role and €2,800 for an Engineering role [6]; the German version states the same values [1]. Under the earlier version 1.0 (effective 2023-02-01), the standard-role budget was €2,000 [7].

**Write-off threshold for separate approval:** Not available in the supplied context. The context states that approval thresholds are defined in POL-018 §3 [9][12], but §3 itself is not provided, and no "write-off threshold" or equivalent figure appears in any block. I cannot infer it.

Note also that exceeding the equipment budget requires written approval from the Head of Workplace & Operations [6] (German: Leitung von Workplace & Operations [1]) — this is a budget-overrun rule, not a write-off threshold.

context_blocks.text:
3. Equipment-Budget

Jede Rollenkategorie hat ein Budget für die anfängliche Equipment-Bestellung. Das Budget umfasst das Laptop, Zubehör und alle zusätzlichen Peripheriegeräte, die Ihre Führungskraft genehmigt. This does not apply to damage caused by gross negligence; such cases are handled individually. **Can I request additional equipment during my employment?**

3. Equipment budget

Each role category has a budget for the initial equipment order. The budget covers the laptop, accessories, and any additional peripheral that your manager approves. If you need something beyond the standard setup, please discuss it with your manager first. We cannot order items that exceed the budget without a written approval from the Head of Workplace & Operations.

The budget values are as follows:

| Role category | Equipment budget | |---------------|------------------| | Standard role | €2,200           | | Engineering role | €2,800        |

The budget is a guideline for the total value of your initial equipment. It is not a personal allowance. You cannot choose a cheaper laptop and use the difference for other purchases. If you have a specific need, for example an ergonomic chair or a second large monitor, your manager can request an exception. Exceptions are reviewed case by case.

4. Refresh cycle

Equipment is refreshed every 36 months. We count from the date the equipment was ordered, not from the date you joined. For example, if you joined in the middle of a refresh cycle, your refresh date may be earlier or later than your work anniversary.

Workplace & Operations tracks refresh dates and reaches out before your refresh is due. You will receive a return label for the old device and a date for the delivery of the new one. Please plan for a short transition period during which you may need to use both devices.

If your equipment breaks outside the refresh cycle and cannot be repaired economically, we will replace it earlier. The replacement does not reset your refresh cycle; you will still receive new equipment at the original refresh date.

Example: Marek, a field solutions engineer working with clients in Poland, received his laptop in March 2024. His refresh is due in March 2027. If his laptop were damaged beyond repair in 2025, he would receive a replacement immediately, but his next refresh would still happen in March 2027.

context_blocks.header: [7] POL-006-v1.0.pdf — Equipment & Hardware Policy > 3. Equipment budget (p. 1–2)
context_blocks.text:
3. Equipment budget

For each new role, Workplace & Operations sets an equipment budget. The equipment budget for a standard role is €2,000. This amount covers the laptop, monitor, and other core items listed in the standard setup. It is intended to be sufficient for a high-quality, reliable setup without requiring you to make a personal contribution.

If your role has specific needs that exceed the standard budget — for example, a field solutions engineer like Marek who needs a rugged device for client sites — your manager can request an exception. The request is reviewed by Workplace & Operations together with the relevant team lead. We ask that you discuss any special needs early in the onboarding process so that the order is not delayed.

The budget is not a personal allowance. You cannot use it to buy items outside the approved equipment list, and you cannot receive the difference in cash. If you have an idea for equipment

that would improve your work but is not on the list, please share it — we are always open to suggestions.

4. Refresh cycle

We keep our equipment current so that you can work efficiently and securely. Equipment is refreshed every 36 months. When your equipment reaches this age, Workplace & Operations will contact you to arrange a replacement.

The refresh process is straightforward. You receive your new device, transfer your files, and return the old one. We handle the data migration carefully to make sure nothing is lost. Platform & Infrastructure will wipe the old device after you have confirmed that your files are moved.

If your equipment is still working well at the refresh point, you may keep it for a little longer. If your equipment fails before the refresh point and cannot be repaired, we will replace it earlier — see §6 for details. If you change roles within the company and your new role requires different equipment, we will adjust your setup at that time rather than waiting for the regular refresh.

1. Questions **Who do I contact when I need to buy something for work?**
Start with your team lead. For anything beyond a small, everyday purchase, your team lead will connect you with the appropriate person in Workplace & Operations. For software or hardware that touches our systems, Platform & Infrastructure reviews the request first. **Is there a formal process?**
Yes. For purchases above the thresholds described in POL-004, you need approval before you order. The policy explains who approves what and which steps to follow. For smaller items, a quick confirmation from your team lead is enough. **What do I do if a supplier asks me to sign something?**
Do not sign. Only people with signing authority per POL-004 may commit Kranich Software to a contract. If a supplier sends you terms, forward them to your team lead or to Workplace & Operations, who will route them correctly. **Which payment method should I use?**
Use the corporate card or the procurement process described in POL-004 whenever possible. Avoid paying out of pocket. If you have an exceptional case, talk to your team lead before you spend anything. Reimbursements are handled through Ledgerly and follow the expense policy. **Can I buy software or an online service myself?**
No. All software subscriptions, even free trials, must go through Platform & Infrastructure. This keeps our tooling consistent and secure. If you sign up for a service without approval, you may be asked to stop using it and to transfer or cancel the account. **How long does approval take?**
It depends on the item and the approver. Simple requests are usually handled promptly. Larger or unusual requests take longer, especially if several teams need to review them. If you are waiting, check in with your team lead rather than chasing the approver directly. **What happens if I order something without approval?**
Orders placed without following POL-004 are not automatically covered. You may be asked to return the item or to cover the cost if it cannot be returned. Example: Marek, a field solutions engineer, once ordered a device directly from a vendor for a client demo.

3. Approvals

Every request needs an approval before we place an order. The level of approval depends on the value of the purchase. POL-018 §3 defines the thresholds precisely; as a rule of thumb, higher values need more senior sign-off.

Your manager approves the business case first. For larger purchases, the responsible department head adds their approval. For the largest purchases, Finance signs off personally. We will tell you who needs to approve your request once we have reviewed it.

You do not need to chase approvers yourself. Ledgerly routes the request automatically and sends reminders. If an approver is away, the request waits until they return or until a delegate steps in. Please factor this into your planning.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, wants to attend a client event. Her manager approves the registration fee. Because the total stays within the lower threshold, no further approval is needed.

If your request is urgent, mention this when you raise it. We will do our best to prioritise, but we

cannot bypass the approval process. Plan ahead where you can.

5. Questions

If you have any question about this policy, start by talking to your manager. They can help you decide whether a purchase is necessary and which approval threshold applies.

For questions about approval thresholds, preferred suppliers, or whether a purchase needs CFO approval, contact Finance. For questions about paying an invoice or reimbursing an expense, use Ledgerly and follow the guidance there.

If you believe this policy is missing something or could be clearer, tell us. We review policies regularly and value feedback from employees. You can send suggestions to people@kranich.example, and they will be forwarded to the policy owner.

Example: Lea, a people operations specialist in Berlin, is unsure whether a team-building activity counts as a purchase under this policy. She asks Finance, and they confirm that it does, because it involves spending company money on an external service. Lea then submits a request with the estimated cost and waits for approval before booking.

Remember: when in doubt, ask. A quick question before you buy can save you from an unapproved expense and a lengthy correction later. We are here to help you get what you need to do your best work.

context_blocks.text:
2. Requesting a purchase

Before you buy anything for Kranich, you must submit a purchase request. Do not place an order, sign a contract, or use your own money before the request is approved, unless you have explicit prior approval from Finance.

To request a purchase, follow these steps:

•  Describe what you need and why. Include the business purpose, for example "a second monitor for the Fleet Insights team" or "a customer workshop in Poland." •  State the estimated cost. If you do not know the exact price, provide your best estimate and explain how you arrived at it. •  Name the supplier you plan to use, if you have one. If you are not sure which supplier to choose, see §4 for preferred suppliers. •  Submit the request through the tool your manager uses for approvals. If you cannot find the right place, ask it-help@kranich.example for guidance.

Once you submit a request, it goes to the right approver based on the approval thresholds in §3. You will receive a notification when a decision is made. If your request is approved, you may proceed with the purchase. If it is declined, the approver will explain why and suggest next steps.

Example: Marek, a field solutions engineer working with clients in Poland, needs a portable projector for an upcoming client demonstration. He submits a request with the estimated cost and the supplier name. His manager approves it the same day, and Marek places the order.

Some purchases do not follow the regular request process. These include expenses you incur while traveling, which you handle through Ledgerly, and purchases made with a corporate card,

whose limits are defined in POL-017 §5. If you use a corporate card for a purchase, you still need to follow this policy for approval before you buy.

If you are unsure whether something qualifies, ask your manager or People & Culture before you spend. **What if my manager and I disagree about a purchase?**
Talk it through first. If you still cannot agree, reach out to People & Culture. We will help find a fair outcome. For guidance on related policies, see §3 of POL-004. Questions about how learning expenses are handled for tax or accounting purposes can be directed to Finance; refer to FIN-RATES-2026 where relevant. **Example:** Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, wants to attend a conference on distributed systems. She checks the agenda with her manager, books her place, and later submits the expense through Ledgerly with her receipt. Her manager had already confirmed the plan, so the reimbursement is processed quickly.

**Was passiert mit meiner Ausstattung, wenn ich Kranich verlasse?**
Sie erhalten Rücksendeanweisungen von Workplace & Operations. Bitte senden Sie die Ausstattung innerhalb der in den Anweisungen genannten Frist zurück. Die Kosten für die Rücksendung übernimmt Kranich. **Muss ich für Reparaturen oder Ersatz zahlen?**
Nein. Kranich übernimmt die Kosten für Reparaturen und Ersatz der Ihnen zugewiesenen Ausstattung. Dies gilt nicht für Schäden durch grobe Fahrlässigkeit; solche Fälle werden individuell behandelt. **Kann ich während meiner Anstellung zusätzliche Ausstattung anfordern?**
Ja. Wenn sich Ihre Bedürfnisse ändern – zum Beispiel, weil Sie in eine Rolle wechseln, die mehr Bildschirmfläche erfordert – reichen Sie eine Anfrage über den in POL-004 beschriebenen Kanal ein. Wir prüfen Anfragen regelmäßig und bemühen uns, zeitnah zu antworten. **Beispiel:** Anna, eine Backend-Engineerin in Lissabon, benötigte einen zweiten Monitor, nachdem sie häufiger Code-Reviews durchführte. Sie reichte eine Anfrage über den Standardprozess ein und erhielt den Monitor innerhalb weniger Tage. **Was ist mit Ausstattung für Besucherinnen und Besucher oder Auftragnehmende?**
Besucherinnen und Besucher sowie kurzfristig eingesetzte Auftragnehmende nutzen Leihgeräte aus dem Büro. Bei längeren Engagements organisiert die verantwortliche Führungskraft dedizierte Ausstattung über denselben Prozess. **Wo finde ich die vollständige Equipment-Richtlinie?**
Siehe POL-004 für die vollständige Richtlinie, einschließlich Anspruchsberechtigung und Ersatzplan. Für Fragen zur Ausstattung auf Reisen siehe FIN-RATES-2026.

Doc Id: POL-006-v1.0 · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2023-02-01 · Owner: Workplace & Operations · Classification: internal

Equipment & Hardware Policy

1. Purpose

At Kranich Software GmbH, we believe that great work starts with the right tools. This policy explains how equipment is provided, maintained, and returned so that everyone — whether you sit in the Ritterstraße office, the Rua do Alecrim office, or work remotely from your home — has a consistent and productive setup.

We want the process to be simple and fair. This policy covers the standard equipment you receive when you join, how the budget works, when equipment is refreshed, and what happens when you leave or when something breaks. If you have questions that are not answered here, reach out to Workplace & Operations or write to it-help@kranich.example.

2. Standard setup

Your standard setup is chosen to match your role. For most employees, this includes a laptop, a monitor, a keyboard, a mouse, a headset, and a docking station. The exact models may vary depending on your team and your work. For example, a backend engineer in Routing Core may receive a more powerful laptop, while a customer success manager may receive a setup optimised for many video calls.

If you work from an office, your equipment is set up at your desk. If you work remotely, we ship the equipment to your home address. In both cases, the equipment remains the property of Kranich Software GmbH. You are responsible for taking reasonable care of it and for keeping it secure. Do not share your laptop or let others use it, even briefly.

Software is installed centrally by Platform & Infrastructure. If you need additional software for your role, submit a request through the usual channel. Peripherals beyond the standard setup — for example, a second monitor or a special chair — can be discussed with your manager and Workplace & Operations.

1. Questions **How much learning budget do I get?**
Every employee has a learning budget of €500 per year. The budget is intended to support your professional development in areas that help you grow in your role at Kranich. **What can I use the budget for?**
You can use it for a wide range of learning activities. This includes conferences, workshops, online courses, books, and professional certifications. It also covers exam fees and membership dues for professional bodies relevant to your work. **Do I need approval before I spend?**
Yes. Please discuss your plan with your manager first. For most expenses, a quick conversation is enough. Your manager will confirm that the activity aligns with your development goals and the team's needs. For larger purchases, such as a multi-day conference, please get written approval in advance. **How do I request reimbursement?**
Submit your expense through Ledgerly, our expenses tool. Attach the receipt and add a short note explaining how the activity supports your development. The Finance team reviews requests promptly. If you need to book travel or accommodation for a learning event, you can also do that through Ledgerly. **What happens if I join Kranich partway through the year?**
The budget is available from your first day of employment. You can use the full amount in your first year, regardless of when you join. **Can I carry unused budget over to the next year?**
No. The budget resets at the start of each calendar year. We encourage you to plan ahead so you can make the most of it. **Are there any restrictions?**
The budget is for learning that is reasonably connected to your role or your professional growth at Kranich. It is not a general personal allowance. Expenses for equipment, software that is already provided by the company, or activities that are primarily recreational are not covered. If you are unsure whether something qualifies, ask your manager or People & Culture before you spend. **What if my manager and I disagree about a purchase?**
Talk it through first. If you still cannot agree, reach out to People & Culture. We will help find a fair outcome. For guidance on related policies, see §3 of POL-004.

Doc Id: FIN-GUIDE-PROCURE · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2025-03-01 · Owner: Finance · Classification: internal

Procurement How-To

1. Purpose

This guide explains how to buy goods and services for Kranich Software. Whether you need a new laptop, a software subscription, or catering for a team offsite, the steps below help you get what you need without delay.

We keep procurement simple. Most requests are routine and follow the same path. For anything unusual, ask us early — Finance is happy to help you find the right way forward.

The spending thresholds that determine who approves what are in POL-018 §3. Please read that section before you start, so you know which approval path applies to your request.

2. Raising a request

Start by raising a request in Ledgerly. Choose the procurement option, describe what you need, and explain why. Attach any quotes or links you already have. The more context you give, the faster we can process your request.

Before you submit, check whether the item is already available internally. For hardware, look at what the company has in stock first. For software, check whether another team already holds a licence you can use. If you are unsure, ask your manager or the relevant team lead.

Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, needs a second monitor for her home setup. She checks the internal hardware list, finds nothing available, and raises a request in Ledgerly with a link to the model she prefers.

Once you submit, you will receive a confirmation. Finance reviews requests promptly. If anything is missing, we will come back to you with clear questions — nothing personal, we simply need the right information to proceed.

5. Questions

If you are unsure whether a purchase is allowed, ask before you buy. For questions about this policy, contact the Finance team through Ledgerly or reach out to it-help@kranich.example for help with the system.

For questions about budget availability, speak to your manager or the Finance contact for your team. They can tell you whether funds are available in the current fiscal year.

If you believe a purchase is necessary but does not fit the standard process, explain the situation in your request. Finance will review it case by case. We would rather answer a question than process a rejected expense later.

Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, wants to attend a conference that is not on the approved list. She submits a request with a note explaining the learning value for her role. Her manager approves it, and the purchase is processed through the standard workflow.

Thank you for following this policy. Your care with procurement keeps our spending transparent and helps Kranich Software grow sustainably.

4. Beantragung Sie beantragen den einmaligen Einrichtungszuschuss über Ledgerly, unser Spesen- und Erstattungstool. Der Prozess ist unkompliziert und dauert nur wenige Minuten. So beantragen Sie den Zuschuss: •  Melden Sie sich mit Ihrem Kranich-Konto bei Ledgerly an. •  Wählen Sie „Neue Ausgabe“ und die Kategorie „Home-Office-Einrichtung“. •  Fügen Sie ein Foto oder PDF Ihrer Quittung bei. Die Quittung muss das Kaufdatum und den Gesamtbetrag zeigen. Quittungen in jeder Währung werden akzeptiert; Ledgerly rechnet sie für Finance um. •  Fügen Sie eine kurze Notiz hinzu, die den Gegenstand beschreibt, zum Beispiel „Bürostuhl“ oder „Schreibtischlampe“. •  Reichen Sie die Ausgabe zur Genehmigung ein. Ihre Führungskraft erhält eine Benachrichtigung zur Genehmigung der Ausgabe. Nach der Genehmigung bearbeitet Finance die Erstattung zeitnah. Das Geld wird je nach Beschäftigungsland über die Gehaltsabrechnung oder eine separate Überweisung auf Ihr Bankkonto überwiesen. Sie können mehrere kleinere Quittungen zusammen einreichen, solange die Summe Ihren verbleibenden Einrichtungszuschuss nicht überschreitet. Sie können auch eine einzelne Quittung über den vollen Betrag einreichen. Sie müssen nicht warten, bis Sie alles gekauft haben. Wenn Sie den Einrichtungszuschuss nach einem Umzug beantragen, wählen Sie dieselbe Ausgabenkategorie und fügen Sie eine Notiz mit dem Hinweis „neue Wohnungseinrichtung“ hinzu, damit Finance dies von Ihrem ersten Antrag unterscheiden kann. Der monatliche Konnektivitätszuschuss muss nicht beantragt werden. Er wird automatisch ab Ihrem ersten vollen Beschäftigungsmonat zu Ihrer monatlichen Gehaltsabrechnung hinzugefügt. Wenn Sie mitten im Monat eintreten, wird der Zuschuss für diesen ersten Teilmomat in die Gehaltsabrechnung des Folgemonats aufgenommen. Beispiel: Anna, eine Backend-Engineerin in Lissabon, hat kurz nach ihrem Eintritt einen Monitorständer und eine Tastatur gekauft.

Equipment & Hardware Policy

1. Purpose

This policy explains how Kranich Software provides equipment to its employees, how equipment is refreshed, and what happens when you leave the company or when hardware is lost or damaged. We want everyone to have the tools they need to do their best work, whether they sit in the Ritterstraße office, the Rua do Alecrim office, or work remotely from home.

This version supersedes version 1.0. The main changes clarify the refresh cycle, the returning process, and how losses are handled. If you have questions after reading this policy, please reach out to Workplace & Operations or your manager.

When you join Kranich, Workplace & Operations arranges your standard setup. The setup includes a laptop, a monitor, a keyboard, a mouse, a headset, and a docking station where needed. We also provide a mobile phone for roles where client contact or on-call duties make one necessary.

Engineering roles receive a more powerful laptop because of the development and testing workloads involved. Doc Id: FIN-GUIDE-EXPENSES · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2025-03-01 · Owner: Finance · Classification: internal

Expense Reports FAQ

1. Purpose

This guide answers the most common questions we hear about expense reports at Kranich Software. It is meant to complement, not replace, the formal policy in POL-004. If you notice a conflict between this FAQ and that policy, the policy wins.

We want the expense process to be simple: you spend money on approved business needs, you submit a report in Ledgerly, and Finance reimburses you promptly. Most questions fall into one of three areas: what to submit, what to attach, and when to do it. We cover all three below.

2. Submitting

When should I submit an expense report? Submit as you go. It is much easier to file a few small reports than to reconstruct a month of spending from memory. A good habit is to log each expense in Ledgerly on the day it happens and submit the report as soon as your trip or activity is complete.

What belongs in an expense report? Business travel, client meetings, approved software, and other costs you incur for your work. If you are unsure whether something qualifies, ask your manager or Finance before you spend. The general rule: if you would not have incurred the cost without your role at Kranich, it is probably reimbursable.

What does not belong? Personal items, upgrades that are not business-related, and anything already covered by a company arrangement. When in doubt, leave it out and ask.

Do I need pre-approval? For routine expenses, no. For larger or unusual purchases, check with your manager first. When in doubt, a quick message is cheaper than a rejected report.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, takes a client to lunch after a workshop. She logs the meal in Ledgerly the same day and submits her report at the end of the week. The report includes the purpose of the meeting and the client's name. That is enough.

Doc Id: POL-018-v1.2 · Version: 1.2 · Effective Date: 2025-11-01 · Supersedes: POL-018 v1.0 · Owner: Finance · Classification: internal

Procurement Policy

1. Purpose

This policy explains how to request, approve, and complete purchases at Kranich Software GmbH. It applies to every employee, regardless of their role or location, whether they work from the Ritterstraße office, the Rua do Alecrim office, or remotely from home.

This version supersedes version 1.0. The previous version did not clearly describe approval thresholds or preferred suppliers; this version does. If you have questions about how this policy applies to a specific situation, contact Finance or your manager.

We want purchasing to be simple and fast, while making sure we spend company money responsibly. We also want to avoid surprises: no one should commit Kranich to a cost without following the steps below. If you are unsure whether something counts as a purchase under this policy, treat it as one and ask.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, wants to buy a new headset for client calls. She checks this policy, follows the request steps, and receives her headset within a few days. The process is straightforward because she planned ahead.

Equipment & Hardware Policy

1. Zweck

Diese Richtlinie erklärt, wie Kranich Software seinen Mitarbeitenden Equipment zur Verfügung stellt, wie Equipment erneuert wird und was passiert, wenn Sie das Unternehmen verlassen oder wenn Hardware verloren geht oder beschädigt wird. Wir möchten, dass alle die Werkzeuge haben, die sie für ihre beste Arbeit benötigen – ob im Ritterstraße-Büro, im Rua-do- Alecrim-Büro oder remote von zu Hause aus.

Diese Version ersetzt Version 1.0. Die wichtigsten Änderungen betreffen den Erneuerungszyklus, den Rückgabeprozess und den Umgang mit Verlusten. Wenn Sie nach dem Lesen dieser Richtlinie Fragen haben, wenden Sie sich bitte an Workplace & Operations oder Ihre Führungskraft.

4. Reforecasts

A reforecast is an updated version of the plan for the current year. It is not a new budget — it is a revised expectation of what we will actually spend. Reforecasts help us keep the plan realistic without changing the accountability of cost-center owners.

Finance decides when a reforecast is needed. Typically, this happens once or twice a year, or sooner if there is a significant change in circumstances — for example, a major new client project or a change in team structure.

When a reforecast is triggered, Finance asks cost-center owners to review their remaining spend for the year and submit updated figures. The process is lighter than the annual planning cycle. You will receive clear instructions and a deadline of a few days.

The reforecast is reviewed by Finance and approved by the leadership team. Once approved, the reforecast becomes the new baseline for variance monitoring for the rest of the year.

Example: Ines Duarte, an engineering manager in Berlin, learns that her team will hire two additional engineers in the second half of the year. She submits a reforecast that reflects the higher personnel costs. Finance approves the update, and variance monitoring continues against the new baseline.

5. Questions

If you have questions about this guide, please reach out to Finance. For questions about your specific cost center, contact your Finance business partner. For general budgeting questions, the Grove intranet has a frequently asked questions page that we keep up to date.

If you notice something in this guide that seems out of date, please let us know. We review our policies regularly and update them when our ways of working change.

Related documents: POL-004 covers expense approval and reimbursement. FIN-RATES-2026 lists the internal charge rates used for cross-team work.

Doc Id: FIN-GUIDE-INVOICES · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2025-03-01 · Owner: Finance · Classification: internal

Supplier Invoice Approval

1. Purpose

This guide explains how supplier invoices are received, approved and paid at Kranich Software GmbH. We work with many external partners — from software vendors and office suppliers to consultants and facility services — and we want to make sure their invoices are handled reliably and without unnecessary delay.

The process described here applies to all invoices from suppliers and vendors that are addressed to Kranich Software GmbH. It covers invoices sent to any of our offices or to individual employees. If you receive an invoice in your inbox or by mail, please forward it to Finance promptly using the address provided in §2, so that we can register it in our system.

2. Receiving invoices

Invoices should be sent to the Finance team by email. If you receive a paper invoice or an invoice attached to an email that was sent to you personally, please forward it to the Finance shared mailbox without editing the attachment.

When Finance receives an invoice, we check that it contains the basic information we need: the supplier name, a clear description of the goods or services, the invoice date, and a reference to the purchase or contract it relates to. If information is missing, we will contact the supplier and ask for a corrected version.

Please do not approve invoices yourself, even if you ordered the goods or services. Your role is to confirm that the work was delivered as expected; the formal approval and payment sit with Finance. If you have questions about whether an invoice is legitimate or expected, contact Finance before the approval clock starts.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, receives an email from a conference organiser with an invoice attached. She forwards it to the Finance mailbox and notes in her reply that the conference was part of her team's customer event. Finance registers the invoice and routes it for approval.

5. Questions

Who do I ask? Start with Ledgerly's help section or your manager. For policy questions, refer to POL-004. For anything about a specific report, contact Finance through Ledgerly, and someone will get back to you.

What about rates and limits? Per-diem rates and category limits are published separately in FIN-RATES-2026. Do not rely on memory or on what a colleague told you last year — check the current rates before you travel or spend.

Can I submit an expense for a colleague? No. Each person submits their own report. If you paid for something together, split it clearly and each person submits their own share with their own receipts.

What if I disagree with a decision? Talk to Finance first. Most issues are simple misunderstandings — a missing receipt, an unclear purpose, or a category that was applied incorrectly. If you still disagree after that conversation, your manager can help escalate it.

Example: Sofia, a product manager in Spain, buys a book for research related to a new Fleet Insights feature. She is unsure whether it counts as a business expense, so she asks Finance before buying. They confirm it does, and she submits the report with the receipt and a note about the feature. No surprises for anyone.

4. Claiming

You claim the one-off setup allowance through Ledgerly, our expenses and reimbursement tool. The process is straightforward and takes only a few minutes.

To claim, follow these steps:

•  Log in to Ledgerly with your Kranich account. •  Select "New expense" and choose the category "Home office setup." •  Attach a photo or PDF of your receipt. The receipt must show the date of purchase and the total amount. A receipt in any currency is accepted; Ledgerly will convert it for Finance. •  Add a short note describing the item, for example "office chair" or "desk lamp." •  Submit the expense for approval.

Your manager will receive a notification to approve the expense. Once approved, Finance processes the reimbursement promptly. The money is transferred to your bank account via payroll or a separate transfer, depending on your country of employment.

You may submit several smaller receipts together, as long as the total does not exceed your remaining setup allowance. You can also submit a single receipt for the full amount. There is no need to wait until you have purchased everything.

If you are claiming the setup allowance after a move, select the same expense category and add a note that says "new home setup" so Finance can distinguish it from your initial claim.

The monthly connectivity allowance does not require a claim. It is added automatically to your payroll each month, starting from your first full month of employment. If you join mid-month, the allowance for that first partial month is included in the following month's payroll.

Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, bought a monitor stand and a keyboard shortly after joining. She submitted both receipts in one claim through Ledgerly and received the reimbursement within a few days.

Doc Id: FIN-GUIDE-BUDGET · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2025-03-01 · Owner: Finance · Classification: internal

Budget Guidelines

1. Purpose

This document explains how budget planning works at Kranich Software GmbH. It covers the annual planning cycle, how we monitor spending against the plan, and when we reforecast. It is written for everyone who owns a budget or contributes to one — from team leads to department heads.

A budget is a promise we make to each other. It lets the company invest in the right things and gives teams clarity on what they can spend. This guide helps you plan realistically, track your spending, and raise concerns early.

2. Planning cycle

Our fiscal year is the calendar year. Planning for the next year starts in the autumn of the current year. Finance coordinates the cycle and publishes a timeline on the Grove intranet ahead of each planning season.

Each team prepares a budget proposal for the coming year. Proposals are based on the team's goals, expected headcount, and planned initiatives. Finance reviews proposals with each team lead and consolidates them into a company-wide plan.

The leadership team approves the final plan before the start of the new year. Once approved, the plan is the baseline against which we measure actual spending. Budgets are set at the cost-center level. Each cost center has a named owner who is responsible for managing spending within that center.

If you are a cost-center owner, you will receive guidance from Finance during the planning cycle. You do not need to build the plan alone — Finance is there to help you estimate costs and challenge assumptions where needed.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, owns the cost center for client workshops. During planning, she works with Finance to estimate travel and material costs for the coming year based on the expected number of workshops.

4. Preferred suppliers

For certain categories, Kranich Software has negotiated agreements with preferred suppliers. You can find the current list on Grove under "Procurement". Using a preferred supplier saves time because contracts and payment terms are already in place.

If you want to use a supplier that is not on the preferred list, that is allowed. Please explain in your purchase request why you chose this supplier. Common reasons include a better feature fit, a more competitive price, or a supplier that is local to the client you are serving.

For software subscriptions, check first whether the tool is already licensed somewhere in the company. The Platform & Infrastructure team maintains a list of approved tools. If you need a new tool, you may also need a security review by the Information Security team. Refer to the security assessment process documented in POL-004 for guidance.

For travel and accommodation, use the booking features in Ledgerly. The system shows options that comply with our travel guidelines. If you book outside the system, reimbursement may be delayed.

Example: Sofia, a product manager working remotely from Spain, needs a new ergonomic keyboard. She checks the preferred supplier list on Grove, finds an approved vendor, and submits her request. Her manager approves it the same day because the amount is within the manager approval threshold.

4. Preferred suppliers

Kranich has agreements with a set of preferred suppliers for common goods and services. Using these suppliers saves time and money because pricing and terms are already negotiated. You are encouraged to check the list of preferred suppliers on Grove before you submit a purchase request.

Preferred suppliers are available for categories such as:

•  Office furniture and equipment •  Software subscriptions and cloud services •  Travel and accommodation, booked through Ledgerly •  Meeting-room and desk equipment, including items for the Perch system

If a preferred supplier offers what you need, choose that supplier. If you believe another supplier is better suited, explain why in your purchase request. For example, a preferred supplier may not offer a product with the specific feature your team needs, or a local supplier may provide faster service in your region.

Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, needs a new keyboard. The preferred supplier

for office equipment delivers to Portugal within a few days and offers the model she wants. She selects that supplier, and her manager approves the request the same day.

For purchases above €20,000, Finance may ask you to obtain quotes from more than one supplier, even if a preferred supplier exists. This helps us confirm that we are getting fair value. If you need help comparing quotes, contact Finance.

The list of preferred suppliers is reviewed regularly and updated when agreements change. If you have a suggestion for a new preferred supplier, share it with Finance. We welcome input from all teams, especially from Customer Success and Go-to-Market, who often know what suppliers work well in the field.

Kranich Software relies on a growing number of external vendors and software-as-a-service tools to run our business. From cloud infrastructure and communication platforms to specialized routing analytics, these tools help our teams work efficiently and serve our customers well. At the same time, every vendor relationship carries cost, security, and operational considerations that we need to manage thoughtfully.

This policy explains how we evaluate, approve, renew, and retire vendor relationships and SaaS subscriptions. It applies to all employees, contractors, and anyone else who procures or manages tools on behalf of Kranich. In most cases, we will still process it, but repeated lateness may require a conversation with your manager. If you have a genuine reason for the delay, just let us know. **Can I claim expenses for remote work?**

question: Which spending limits trigger your supervisor's sign-off versus the finance chief's authorization?
answer_text:
The specific monetary limits are **not available in the supplied context**. No block states the threshold values for manager/supervisor sign-off or CFO authorization; those are defined in POL-018 §3, which is not included here [2].

What the context does support:

- The approval level depends on the value of the purchase, with higher values needing more senior sign-off; POL-018 §3 defines the thresholds precisely [2].
- The escalation route: your manager approves the business case first, the responsible department head adds approval for larger purchases, and Finance signs off personally for the largest purchases [2].
- Questions about whether a purchase needs **CFO approval** should be directed to Finance [1]. The v1.2 policy supersedes v1.0, noting that the previous version did not clearly describe approval thresholds [21].

So: the ordering (manager → department head → Finance/CFO) is supported, but the numeric spending limits that trigger each level are not available in these context blocks.

5. Fragen

Wenn Sie Fragen zu dieser Richtlinie haben, sprechen Sie zunächst mit Ihrer Führungskraft. Sie kann Ihnen helfen zu entscheiden, ob ein Einkauf notwendig ist und welche Genehmigungsschwelle gilt.

Bei Fragen zu Genehmigungsschwellen, bevorzugten Lieferanten oder ob ein Einkauf die Genehmigung des CFO erfordert, wenden Sie sich an Finance. Bei Fragen zur Bezahlung einer Rechnung oder zur Erstattung einer Ausgabe nutzen Sie Ledgerly und folgen Sie den dortigen Hinweisen.

Wenn Sie glauben, dass diese Richtlinie etwas vermissen lässt oder klarer sein könnte, teilen Sie uns das mit. Wir überprüfen Richtlinien regelmäßig und schätzen Feedback von Mitarbeitenden. Sie können Vorschläge an people@kranich.example senden, und sie werden an die verantwortliche Person für die Richtlinie weitergeleitet.

Beispiel: Lea, eine People Operations Spezialistin in Berlin, ist unsicher, ob eine Teambuilding- Aktivität unter diese Richtlinie als Einkauf fällt. Sie fragt Finance, und diese bestätigen, dass es so ist, weil es die Ausgabe von Unternehmensgeldern für einen externen Dienst beinhaltet. Lea reicht dann eine Anfrage mit den geschätzten Kosten ein und wartet auf die Genehmigung, bevor sie bucht.

Denken Sie daran: Im Zweifel fragen Sie nach. Eine kurze Frage vor dem Kauf kann Sie vor einer nicht genehmigten Ausgabe und einer langwierigen Korrektur später bewahren. Wir sind hier, um Ihnen zu helfen, das zu bekommen, was Sie für Ihre beste Arbeit benötigen.

6. Fragen

Wenn Sie Fragen zu dieser Richtlinie haben, wenden Sie sich bitte an die Finanzabteilung. Bei Fragen dazu, wie Sie eine Ausgabe erfassen oder was als geschäftliche Kosten gilt, lesen Sie POL-004.

Wenn Sie vermuten, dass Ihre Karte missbraucht wurde, oder Sie eine verdächtige Transaktion bemerken, kontaktieren Sie security@kranich.example. Bei verlorenen oder beschädigten Karten oder technischen Problemen mit dem Portal des Kartenanbieters wenden Sie sich an it- help@kranich.example.

Bei Fragen dazu, ob Ihre Rolle für eine Karte infrage kommt, sprechen Sie zuerst mit Ihrer Führungskraft. Wenn Sie dringend eine Karte benötigen, etwa für eine anstehende Reise, bitten Sie Ihre Führungskraft, den Antrag bei der Finanzabteilung zu kennzeichnen, damit er zeitnah bearbeitet werden kann.

Beispiel: Sofia, eine Produktmanagerin im Fleet Insights Team, die remote aus Spanien arbeitet, fragt sich, ob sie die Corporate Card für den Kauf eines neuen Headsets für ihr Homeoffice-Setup verwenden darf. Sie klärt dies mit ihrer Führungskraft, die bestätigt, dass dies eine genehmigte Homeoffice-Ausgabe innerhalb des Einzeltransaktionslimits ist. Sofia tätigt den Kauf und reicht den Beleg beim Abgleich ein.

Die Finanzabteilung überprüft diese Richtlinie regelmäßig, um sie an unsere Arbeitsweise

anzupassen. Wenn Sie Vorschläge haben, wie sie klarer oder praktischer gestaltet werden kann, freuen wir uns über Ihr Feedback.

Expense Reports FAQ

1. Purpose

This guide answers the most common questions we hear about expense reports at Kranich Software. It is meant to complement, not replace, the formal policy in POL-004. If you notice a conflict between this FAQ and that policy, the policy wins.

We want the expense process to be simple: you spend money on approved business needs, you submit a report in Ledgerly, and Finance reimburses you promptly. Most questions fall into one of three areas: what to submit, what to attach, and when to do it. We cover all three below.

2. Submitting

When should I submit an expense report? Submit as you go. It is much easier to file a few small reports than to reconstruct a month of spending from memory. A good habit is to log each expense in Ledgerly on the day it happens and submit the report as soon as your trip or activity is complete.

What belongs in an expense report? Business travel, client meetings, approved software, and other costs you incur for your work. If you are unsure whether something qualifies, ask your manager or Finance before you spend. The general rule: if you would not have incurred the cost without your role at Kranich, it is probably reimbursable.

What does not belong? Personal items, upgrades that are not business-related, and anything already covered by a company arrangement. When in doubt, leave it out and ask.

Do I need pre-approval? For routine expenses, no. For larger or unusual purchases, check with your manager first. When in doubt, a quick message is cheaper than a rejected report.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, takes a client to lunch after a workshop. She logs the meal in Ledgerly the same day and submits her report at the end of the week. The report includes the purpose of the meeting and the client's name. That is enough.

4. Receipts and reconciliation

Every charge on the corporate card must be reconciled. You are responsible for submitting receipts and a short explanation for each transaction within the timeframe described in POL-004 §6. Do not wait for a reminder.

For each transaction, provide:

•  A clear description of what was purchased •  The business reason •  The receipt, if one was issued

If a receipt is missing, write a short note explaining why. For example, a taxi ride may not produce a paper receipt; in that case, note the date, route, and purpose.

Your manager approves your reconciled expenses. Finance reviews them afterwards. If something is unclear, Finance will reach out to you directly. Please respond promptly so that reconciliation can be completed.

If you notice an error on your statement, such as a duplicate charge or an incorrect amount, contact Finance before the deadline in POL-004 §6 has passed.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, takes a client to dinner. She keeps the itemized receipt and submits it with a note saying which client and which project the dinner supported. Her manager approves it, and Finance closes the transaction.

In most cases, we will still process it, but repeated lateness may require a conversation with your manager. If you have a genuine reason for the delay, just let us know. **Can I claim expenses for remote work?**
Occasional costs like a coffee shop visit for a client call may be claimed, but ongoing home-office costs are not covered under this policy. For recurring needs, please check the relevant policy on Grove. **Who approves my expenses?**
Your direct manager approves your report. For larger amounts, finance reviews it as well. If you have questions about a specific submission, reach out to people@kranich.example. **What if my expense is denied?**
You will receive a note explaining why. Common reasons include missing receipts or personal items. You can adjust the report and resubmit, or speak with your manager if you believe the decision was made in error. **Are there special rules for client entertainment?**

Reimbursement rates for per-diem items follow FIN-RATES-2026. If your travel takes you to a country not listed there, contact finance before your trip to confirm the applicable rate. **Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, traveled to Berlin for a workshop. 2. Requesting a purchase

Before you buy anything for Kranich, you must submit a purchase request. Do not place an order, sign a contract, or use your own money before the request is approved, unless you have explicit prior approval from Finance.

To request a purchase, follow these steps:

•  Describe what you need and why. Include the business purpose, for example "a second monitor for the Fleet Insights team" or "a customer workshop in Poland." •  State the estimated cost. If you do not know the exact price, provide your best estimate and explain how you arrived at it. •  Name the supplier you plan to use, if you have one. If you are not sure which supplier to choose, see §4 for preferred suppliers. •  Submit the request through the tool your manager uses for approvals. If you cannot find the right place, ask it-help@kranich.example for guidance.

Once you submit a request, it goes to the right approver based on the approval thresholds in §3. You will receive a notification when a decision is made. If your request is approved, you may proceed with the purchase. If it is declined, the approver will explain why and suggest next steps.

Example: Marek, a field solutions engineer working with clients in Poland, needs a portable projector for an upcoming client demonstration. He submits a request with the estimated cost and the supplier name. His manager approves it the same day, and Marek places the order.

Some purchases do not follow the regular request process. These include expenses you incur while traveling, which you handle through Ledgerly, and purchases made with a corporate card,

whose limits are defined in POL-017 §5. If you use a corporate card for a purchase, you still need to follow this policy for approval before you buy.

3. Using the card

Use the corporate card only for business purposes. Personal purchases are never allowed, even if you intend to reimburse the company later.

Acceptable uses include:

•  Travel costs such as flights, trains, and hotels •  Meals with clients or during business travel •  Business software and online services

•  Office supplies and equipment, with manager approval •  Conference fees and related event costs

Before making a purchase above a modest amount, check with your manager if you are unsure whether the expense is justified. For recurring charges, such as a monthly software subscription, make sure the subscription is already approved by your team lead.

You are responsible for keeping your card details secure. Do not store the card number in unapproved tools. If you suspect fraud or loss, contact security@kranich.example immediately and then it-help@kranich.example for a replacement.

Do not use the card for cash advances. Do not use it to pay fines, penalties, or personal legal fees. If you accidentally use the card for a personal expense, flag it in the reconciliation tool right away so Finance can arrange a correction.

Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, buys a book about a new programming framework for her team's library. That is a reasonable team expense. She also picks up a coffee for herself on the way back to her home office; she pays for that with her own money, not the corporate card.

Doc Id: POL-018-v1.0 · Version: 1.0 · Effective Date: 2024-02-01 · Owner: Finance · Classification: internal

Procurement Policy

1. Purpose

This policy explains how to purchase goods and services on behalf of Kranich Software GmbH. Whether you need a new monitor for your home office, a software license for your team, or catering for a customer workshop, this policy helps you get what you need quickly and responsibly.

We want every purchase to be transparent, fair, and aligned with our budget. By following the steps below, you help Finance keep accurate records and ensure we spend company money wisely.

This policy applies to all employees, regardless of where they work. If you are based in Berlin, Lisbon, or working remotely from another country, the same rules apply.

2. Requesting a purchase

Before you buy anything, check whether the item or service is already available. For software, look in the internal tool catalog on Grove. For hardware, ask your manager or the Workplace team — we may have spare equipment in the Berlin or Lisbon offices.

If the item is not available internally, submit a purchase request through Ledgerly. You will need to describe what you are buying, why you need it, and which budget it should be charged to. Attach a quote or a link to the product page so Finance can verify the price.

Do not place an order before your request is approved. If you order first and ask later, the expense may not be reimbursed, and you could be personally liable for the cost.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, wants to send a welcome package to a new client. She checks Grove for a preferred supplier, submits a request in Ledgerly with the item link, and waits for approval before placing the order.

1. Questions **How much learning budget do I get?**
Every employee has a learning budget of €500 per year. The budget is intended to support your professional development in areas that help you grow in your role at Kranich. **What can I use the budget for?**
You can use it for a wide range of learning activities. This includes conferences, workshops, online courses, books, and professional certifications. It also covers exam fees and membership dues for professional bodies relevant to your work. **Do I need approval before I spend?**
Yes. Please discuss your plan with your manager first. For most expenses, a quick conversation is enough. Your manager will confirm that the activity aligns with your development goals and the team's needs. For larger purchases, such as a multi-day conference, please get written approval in advance. **How do I request reimbursement?**
Submit your expense through Ledgerly, our expenses tool. Attach the receipt and add a short note explaining how the activity supports your development. The Finance team reviews requests promptly. If you need to book travel or accommodation for a learning event, you can also do that through Ledgerly. **What happens if I join Kranich partway through the year?**
The budget is available from your first day of employment. You can use the full amount in your first year, regardless of when you join. **Can I carry unused budget over to the next year?**
No. The budget resets at the start of each calendar year. We encourage you to plan ahead so you can make the most of it. **Are there any restrictions?**
The budget is for learning that is reasonably connected to your role or your professional growth at Kranich. It is not a general personal allowance. Expenses for equipment, software that is already provided by the company, or activities that are primarily recreational are not covered. If you are unsure whether something qualifies, ask your manager or People & Culture before you spend. **What if my manager and I disagree about a purchase?**
Talk it through first. If you still cannot agree, reach out to People & Culture. We will help find a fair outcome. For guidance on related policies, see §3 of POL-004.

5. Questions

If you are unsure whether a specific expense is covered, please ask your manager or the Finance team before you travel. For practical help with booking or with Ledgerly, contact it- help@kranich.example. For questions about the rates themselves, please reach out to Finance directly. We want travel to be straightforward, so you can focus on the work with our customers.

Procurement Policy

1. Purpose

This policy explains how to request, approve, and complete purchases at Kranich Software GmbH. It applies to every employee, regardless of their role or location, whether they work from the Ritterstraße office, the Rua do Alecrim office, or remotely from home.

This version supersedes version 1.0. The previous version did not clearly describe approval thresholds or preferred suppliers; this version does. If you have questions about how this policy applies to a specific situation, contact Finance or your manager.

We want purchasing to be simple and fast, while making sure we spend company money responsibly. We also want to avoid surprises: no one should commit Kranich to a cost without following the steps below. If you are unsure whether something counts as a purchase under this policy, treat it as one and ask.

Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, wants to buy a new headset for client calls. She checks this policy, follows the request steps, and receives her headset within a few days. The process is straightforward because she planned ahead.

4. Reforecasts

A reforecast is an updated version of the plan for the current year. It is not a new budget — it is a revised expectation of what we will actually spend. Reforecasts help us keep the plan realistic without changing the accountability of cost-center owners.

Finance decides when a reforecast is needed. Typically, this happens once or twice a year, or sooner if there is a significant change in circumstances — for example, a major new client project or a change in team structure.

When a reforecast is triggered, Finance asks cost-center owners to review their remaining spend for the year and submit updated figures. The process is lighter than the annual planning cycle. You will receive clear instructions and a deadline of a few days.

The reforecast is reviewed by Finance and approved by the leadership team. Once approved, the reforecast becomes the new baseline for variance monitoring for the rest of the year.

Example: Ines Duarte, an engineering manager in Berlin, learns that her team will hire two additional engineers in the second half of the year. She submits a reforecast that reflects the higher personnel costs. Finance approves the update, and variance monitoring continues against the new baseline.

5. Questions

If you have questions about this guide, please reach out to Finance. For questions about your specific cost center, contact your Finance business partner. For general budgeting questions, the Grove intranet has a frequently asked questions page that we keep up to date.

If you notice something in this guide that seems out of date, please let us know. We review our policies regularly and update them when our ways of working change.

Related documents: POL-004 covers expense approval and reimbursement. FIN-RATES-2026 lists the internal charge rates used for cross-team work.

context_blocks.header: [23] ENG-ADR-04.pdf — ADR-04: Pipeline time budget > 3. Decision (p. 1–2)
context_blocks.text:
3. Decision

The full pipeline must finish within 68 minutes. This budget covers the complete run from the moment a commit is picked up to the moment artifacts are ready for deployment. It includes compilation, unit and integration tests, container builds, and the packaging steps.

We define "full pipeline" as the end-to-end sequence that runs for a merge to the main branch. Short-lived checks, such as a quick lint on a pull request, are not part of this budget. However, any step that runs in the main-branch pipeline counts toward the 68 minutes, regardless of which team owns the step.

To make the budget enforceable, we add a monitoring alert that fires when a pipeline run approaches the ceiling. If a run exceeds the budget, the pipeline fails and the owning team receives a notification. The team can then investigate and either optimize the step or open a request to exempt that particular pipeline from the budget. Exemptions are reviewed by Platform & Infrastructure and are meant to be temporary; we expect teams to treat an

exemption as a prompt to refactor rather than as a permanent allowance.

We also commit to reviewing the budget on a regular cadence. If the product roadmap introduces work that fundamentally changes the build shape, we may revisit this decision, but any change to the 68 minutes will go through the same architecture review process as this document.

6. Questions

If you have questions about this policy, contact the Finance team. They can help you understand whether a purchase is appropriate, how to reconcile a transaction, or what to do if your card is lost or stolen.

For questions about booking travel or submitting expenses, refer to the guidance in Ledgerly or contact it-help@kranich.example for technical issues with the tool.

If you believe you need a corporate card but do not have one, speak to your manager first. They will confirm that your role requires it and will submit a request to Finance on your behalf.

We want this policy to be easy to follow. If something is unclear, please ask rather than guess. The Finance team is happy to help.

6. Submitting expenses

Submit your expense report through Ledgerly. Attach a receipt for every expense above the threshold described in the current Expense Rates sheet (FIN-RATES-2026). For expenses below that threshold, a receipt is not required, but you must still list the expense and its purpose.

Expense reports are due within 30 calendar days after the trip ends. If you submit later, we may not be able to reimburse you, and we will ask you to explain the delay. Submitting on time keeps our accounting accurate and helps Finance close the books each month.

For each expense, add a short description that explains the business purpose. Write something like "Taxi from Lisbon airport to hotel for Routing Core offsite" rather than just "Taxi". If an expense is unusual or the purpose is not obvious, add a sentence of context.

Your manager approves the report first, and Finance reviews it after. If Finance has questions, they will reach out to you through Ledgerly. Once approved, reimbursement is paid through payroll on the next scheduled run.

Keep your receipts for your own records even after you submit. Ledgerly stores the attachments, but it is good practice to keep a copy until the reimbursement lands in your account.

Example: Lea, a people operations specialist in Berlin, returns from a two-day recruiting event in Lisbon. Within a week of returning, she submits her report in Ledgerly with receipts for her taxi rides and a note explaining the purpose of each. Her manager approves the report, and Finance processes it in the next payroll run.

context_blocks.header: [26] FIN-GUIDE-YEAREND.pdf — Year-End Close Guide > 3. What we need from you (p. 1–2)
context_blocks.text: 3. What we need from you Most of the year-end close is handled by Finance. However, there are a few things that need input from people across the company. Here is what we ask of you. Submit your expenses promptly. If you have any business expenses from the past year that you have not yet claimed, please submit them in Ledgerly before the close begins. Expenses submitted after the close starts may have to wait until the following year. Check your receipts and submit anything outstanding as soon as you can. Confirm your travel bookings. If you travelled for work near the end of the year, please make sure your bookings in Ledgerly are finalised. Cancel any trips you did not take so that we do not carry unused bookings into the new year. Review your leave balance. Your leave balance is tracked in Fern. Before the year ends, please check that your recorded balance looks right to you. If something seems off, contact People & Culture promptly. Once the year closes, correcting historical leave data becomes much harder. Approve pending requests. If you are a manager, please review and approve any pending expense reports, leave requests, or other financial items from your team before the close. Approvals that sit open during the close slow everyone down. Tell us about anything unusual. If you know of a payment that is coming in or going out around the turn of the year, or if you have signed a contract with a client or vendor that spans the year boundary, please let Finance know. A short note is enough. It helps us record things in the right year. Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, realises in early December that she has a few business meals from November that she never claimed. She submits them in Ledgerly right away, before the close begins. She also checks her leave balance in Fern and confirms that it matches her own records. Nothing else is outstanding, so she needs to do nothing further for the close. Example: Deniz, a customer success manager in Berlin, is a manager. Before the year ends, she goes through her team's pending approvals in Ledgerly and Fern and clears them all. She also notices that one of her team members has an open travel booking for a client visit that was cancelled.

context_blocks.header: [31] FIN-GUIDE-INVOICES.pdf — Supplier Invoice Approval > 3. Approval SLA (p. 1–2)
context_blocks.text:
3. Approval SLA

Supplier invoices are approved within 8 business days of receipt. The clock starts on the day Finance confirms receipt of a complete invoice. If we need to ask the supplier for missing details, the clock restarts once we have the corrected version.

Approval follows a simple route. Finance first checks the invoice against the relevant purchase order or contract. If the invoice matches, Finance approves it. If the invoice relates to a service or project managed by a specific team, Finance may ask that team's lead to confirm the work was delivered before approval is granted.

In practice, most invoices are approved well within the target. Invoices that require additional checks — for example, because the supplier is new or the amount is unusual for that vendor — may take longer, and we will keep the requester informed if that happens.

Example: Marek, a field solutions engineer working with clients in Poland, arranges a training room rental for a client workshop. The hotel sends the invoice to Marek directly. He forwards it to Finance on a Monday. Finance confirms receipt the same day, checks it against the booking confirmation, and the invoice is approved within the week.

4. Payment runs

Once an invoice is approved, it is scheduled for the next payment run. Finance processes payments on a regular cycle, usually every few weeks. Approved invoices are grouped into batches and paid together to keep bank charges low and to make cash flow predictable.

If a supplier asks about payment status, please do not promise a specific date. Refer them to Finance, or let Finance know that the supplier has been in touch. We will confirm the payment date once the invoice is in a payment batch.

Example: Anna, a backend engineer in Lisbon, orders a new external hard drive for testing. The supplier sends the invoice to her, she forwards it to Finance, and the invoice is approved in good time. When the supplier emails Anna a week later asking when payment will arrive, she replies that Finance handles payments and offers to connect them.
